div.head: Ine 63
div.ab: CVII. Gif gesiðcund mon fare, þonne mot he habban his gerefan mid him ⁊ his smið ⁊ his cildfestran.
CVII. Gif gesiðcund mon fare, ðonne mot he habban his gerefan mid him ⁊ his smið ⁊ his cildfestran.
Be gesiðcundes mannes fare. Gyf gesiðcund man fare, ðonne mot he habban his gerefan mid him ⁊ his smið ⁊ his cildfestran.
Si homo siþcundus abeat (transmigret), liceat ei habere prepositum suum (socios suos) secum et fabrum et nutricem suam.
[Be gesiðcundes mannes fare.] Gif gesiðcund mon fare, þonne mot he habban his gerefan mid him ⁊ his smið ⁊ his cildfestran.
{CVII} Gif gesiðcunde mon fare, þonne mot he habban his gerefan mid him ⁊ his smið ⁊ his cildfestran.
Wenn ein Mann vom Gefolgsadel [aus dem Lehngut] abzieht, dann darf er seinen Amtmann und seinen Schmied und seine Kinderamme mit sich nehmen.
If a man of the retainer nobility moves away [from his estate], then he may take his reeve and his smith and his children’s nurse with him.
If a nobleman moves his residence he may take with him his reeve, his smith, and his children's nurse.
If a gesith-born man moves elsewhere, he may then have with him his reeve and his smith and his children’s nurse.
If a noble man moves [to a different district], he may take with him his reeve and his smith and his children’s nurse.

socios Q, durch häufigen Lesefehler geferan. — Vgl. Vogt 13; Herrschaftsgut 5. Vermutlich braucht der Gefolgsadel den Verwalter fürs nächste zu übernehmende Leihegut

Metal-worker in general; see Gl Schmied

Vgl. Gl Amme; Erziehung 1. Die Endung -estre verbietet, an einen Pfleger zu denken. — Dem Herrenverräter gleich gilt, wer des Herrn Kinderamme beschläft bei Britton (Ende 13. Jhs.) c. 22 (I 41), zitiert von Price für die Wichtigkeit der Person. Vgl. c. 1140: Cum familia militis . . de una mansione ad aliam deberet mansionem militis tendere, matrona, quae liberos eius educare consueverat, altrix militaris prolis usw.; Osbert de Clara ed. Anstruther 175. — Robertson Hist. essays 200 denkt an die Adoptivmutter des Gutsbesitzers; allein diese Art der Erziehung (s. Gl 4) steht wohl für Ines Zeit nicht fest. Auch konnte deren Übersiedeln zum Pflegesohn, ihre Gebundenheit ans Gut, und ihr Überleben seines Leihewechsels nur ein Zusammentreffen von Ausnahmefällen sein, das eines Gesetzes schwerlich bedurfte

Cf. Gl Amme; Erziehung 1. The ending -estre rules out thinking of a male fosterer. — In Britton (end of the 13th cent.) c. 22 (I 41), whoever lies with his lord’s children’s nurse is treated as equal to a traitor to his lord; cited by Price for the importance of the person. Cf. c. 1140: Cum familia militis . . de una mansione ad aliam deberet mansionem militis tendere, matrona, quae liberos eius educare consueverat, altrix militaris prolis etc.; Osbert de Clara ed. Anstruther 175. — Robertson Hist. essays 200 thinks of the landholder’s adoptive mother; but this kind of upbringing (see Gl 4) is probably not established for Ine’s time. Moreover, her moving to her foster-son, her being bound to the estate, and her outliving his change of leasehold could only have been a coincidence of exceptional cases, which would hardly have needed a law

Alle drei müssen also ausser in diesem Ausnahmefall ans Herrschaftsgut gebunden sein. Eine falsche Urk. 13.—14. Jhs. verleiht Croylandiae manerium cum appendiciis, sc. prepositum, fabrum; Reeve, häufig ein Villan, und Schmied gelten also noch um 1300 als gutshörig

All three must therefore, except in this exceptional case, be bound to the manorial estate. A spurious charter of the 13th–14th cent. grants Croylandiae manerium cum appendiciis, sc. prepositum, fabrum; the reeve, frequently a villein, and the smith are thus still regarded c. 1300 as bound to the manor
With B. and T. and Liebermann I have taken -festran as fem. (nom. -festre). It might however be a masc. noun (nom. -festra) meaning ‘fosterer.’
